Subject: Post-call recap + next tests: Private VPC / air-gap feasibility

Hi Samir / Jenna - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary requirement: private VPC deployment with strict egress controls and the ability to run air-gapped for regulated workloads.
- Main competitor touchpoint: you're also evaluating hyperscaler-managed inference (GCP Vertex / AWS SageMaker) and one other inference API.
- Key success criteria: private control plane option, zero egress for model inferencing, SOC2 artifacts for security/compliance, and a short POC to validate latency and networking.

How Redwood differentiates (short):
- Private control plane option: customers can run a customer-managed control plane (VPC-to-VPC peering or private link) or opt for an on-prem control plane in air-gapped mode - means no management plane egress by default.
- Operational parity: same API surface across hosted/dedicated/private so your app code doesn't change between POC and prod.
- Cost/perf controls: flexible batching/quantization settings and observability to tune cost vs latency (helps vs generic hyperscaler endpoints).

Proposed next tests (we can run these in a 2-3 week POC):
1) Network connectivity test: validate whether a private endpoint (PrivateLink/VPC peering) can reach our dedicated POC nodes. Marcus will provide a minimal firewall/IP allowlist.
2) Control plane connectivity: test customer-managed control plane variant vs Redwood-managed control plane (we'll show you the steps to flip).
3) Air-gap feasibility: walkthrough on what an air-gapped deployment would require (on-prem install + artifact exchange). This is heavier lift; we propose a week-long technical spike.
4) Security artifacts: we attached a SOC2 evidence checklist and can share redacted reports under NDA if needed.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-architecture.pdf (Marcus' network sketch), SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx (security checklist).

Next step: Marcus will send the networking checklist and proposed test timeline. Can we lock in a 30-45m call next Wed (Sep 29) for the technical kickoff? Jenna / Samir - does 11am PT work?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Hi all - attaching the network sketch and a short checklist for the connectivity test. High level steps below; see attachment for diagrams.

Proposed network checklist (minimal):
- Provide a list of outbound IPs you can allow (we'll provide a static set for the POC) or prefer PrivateLink/VPC Peering.
- For PrivateLink: create an interface endpoint in your VPC and share the endpoint id and route table.
- If you require zero egress for inference: we recommend the on-prem air-gapped deployment path. For this spike we can simulate egress-disabled mode by hosting a dedicated instance inside your VPC with NAT disabled and verifying telemetry flows locally.
- Ports: allow TCP 443 for control-plane bootstrap (if using customer-managed control plane) or provide offline artifact exchange instructions for full air-gap.
- NTP and cert distribution: we'll need a way to distribute certs (either via your internal PKI or a one-time signed bundle).

Timeline estimate for the spike:
- Network prep & whiteboard: 2 full days (your network/security + our SE).
- Control plane flip + deploy to dedicated instance: 1-2 days.
- Air-gap technical spike (on-prem install + validation): 5-7 days depending on access & approvals.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-architecture.pdf

I'll open a shared folder for logs and we'll capture the exact test plan. Marcus
